absent: Bit positions and numeric values of shadow entry masks, role fields, and paging level constants.
Implementation of remote flush, zap, yield, and request primitives referenced by synchronization paths.
Full structure definitions for virtual machine, virtual CPU, memory slot, and shadow page objects.
Huge page level selection and large page policy beyond the single disallow observation.
Recovery behavior for nested paging inconsistencies and allocation failures outside the shown checks.
Lifetime and reclamation of invalidated TDP roots after publication.

findings.text: Host operation that clears write permission for a guest frame in every valid TDP root of a slot address space and indicates whether any mapping was altered.
Per-root write protection only touches present leaf mappings at or above a minimum level, clears architectural and shadow writable attributes, and treats an already protected entry as completion.
Valid-root iteration is scoped to a virtual machine and an address-space identifier and selects only roots in valid state.
Split shadow entry update publishes the upper half before the lower half with an ordering barrier so observers never see a transient present entry during activation.
A leaf entry change requires remote TLB maintenance exactly when it loses host-writable status.
Guest-frame remote flush helper expands a frame and level into an aligned range sized for that level.
Write-tracking activation for a guest frame records tracking state, forbids large mappings for that frame, applies write protection, and requests remote flush only when protection changed state.
Shadow page creation is reflected in both a virtual-machine counter and host pagetable accounting.
MMU object cache provides a pooled object when available, otherwise allocates an atomic accounted object, and never yields an empty result.

TDP root acquisition for a virtual CPU reuses an existing root with matching role when possible and otherwise creates, initializes and publishes a new root before installing its host address into the active or mirror slot.
New TDP shadow page obtains both its descriptor and its table storage from per-virtual-CPU caches.
Reference acquisition on a TDP root succeeds only while the root remains live.

Shadow root provisioning covers invisible guest root fallback, early guest table sampling, one-time metadata preparation, and selection between a single 64-bit root and a legacy-rooted hierarchy with upper levels as needed.
Guest page directory retrieval uses a direct control-register read for the default accessor under a hardening configuration and otherwise delegates to the walker accessor.
First shadow root preparation is idempotent, performs hash and per-slot metadata allocation once, tolerates retry without freeing partial results, and publishes completion with release ordering.
Shadow page hash allocation is skipped when already present and otherwise installs a zeroed accounted table with ordering that pairs with acquire-side readers.
Per-slot write-tracking storage allocation sizes the structure from the slot page count.
Dummy root address derives from the zero frame shifted to page granularity.
Guest frame visibility query resolves the frame to a slot and accepts only user slots that are not marked invalid.
Visibility requires an existing slot whose identifier lies in the user range and whose invalid marker is clear.
Auxiliary upper tables for shadowing 32-bit guest paging with 64-bit host paging are created once as cleared pages and rejected when host paging mode or existing partial state is inconsistent.
Root synchronization entry skips direct or invalid configurations, discards cached emulation state, and reconciles either a single 64-bit hierarchy or each valid legacy root.
Unsynchronized-root test orders permission observation before flag observation and treats invalid, dummy, or descriptor-less roots as synchronized.

Unsynchronized subtree reconciliation alternates between protecting tracked frames and unlinking plus synchronizing pages, flushing as needed, and either yielding under contention or deferring completion through a rescheduling request.
Virtual-CPU scoped frame protection resolves the frame through the virtual CPU view and enforces protection at small-page granularity.
Obsolete-root reclamation examines current and retained roots for a virtual machine and releases those identified as stale.
Staleness evaluation treats invalid addresses as fresh, descriptor-less roots as stale, and otherwise defers to shadow-page staleness.

Process-context identifier handling returns masked control-register bits only when the host enables the feature, with active queries sampling the current control register and address-tag bits gated by guest capability.

Passthrough permission refresh is bypassed without two-dimensional paging or for nested address translation, otherwise it resynchronizes cached write-protect state and rebuilds paging metadata when the live value differs.
TDP root descriptor carries a role value, a reference count, list linkage for root enumeration, and table storage whose host address is installed into MMU state.
MMU root state holds a host address and guest directory snapshot, plus optional legacy and upper-level tables for older guest modes.
Shadow page tracks its guest frame, synchronization flags for itself and descendants, and linkage used by unsynchronized walks.
Guest-frame write protection across TDP roots requires exclusive MMU ownership and internally uses read-side critical sections for table walks.
Write-track activation requires exclusive MMU ownership together with either slot-lock ownership or source-read protection.
TDP root lookup uses shared MMU protection for the fast path and a dedicated pages spinlock for creation, with revalidation after each acquisition to handle races.
Shadow root construction and synchronization mutate shared MMU state under exclusive MMU protection, with guest memory sampling performed before acquisition when it may sleep.
First-use metadata initialization serializes on the architecture slot mutex and relies on double-checked completion to avoid redundant work.
A root installed after protection is released may already be invalidated, so consumption must be guarded by an obsolescence check and a held reference that prevents premature freeing.
Cache exhaustion and hash allocation failure are terminal for the requesting path and must be propagated rather than retried silently.
Legacy shadow hierarchy uses four root slots per virtual CPU.
Newly published TDP root starts with a pair of references covering both the requester and virtual machine retention until invalidation.
